beats.say: All bees die after they sting you. Nope. Most of them can sting again.
The ones that die are worker honeybees, and mainly when they sting something with thick, stretchy skin, like you.
Their stinger has tiny backward barbs. In skin like ours it gets stuck, and when the bee pulls away, the stinger stays behind. The bee doesn't survive that.
But when a honeybee stings another insect, the stinger can usually slide back out, and the bee flies off fine.
Bumblebees and wasps have smooth stingers, so they can sting you over and over. And male bees? They can't sting at all. Zero weapons. Just vibes.
So that bee isn't on a suicide mission. It's just having a really bad day because of your arm.
beats.text:
NOT A MISSION.
A BAD DAY.

beats.say: The full episode, with even more myths, is on the channel.
